summary: DLMF 24.16 Generalizations: For \ell=0,1,2,\dotsc , Bernoulli and Euler polynomials of order \ell are defined respectively by
body: NIST DLMF section 24.16 (Generalizations) says: "For \ell=0,1,2,\dotsc , Bernoulli and Euler polynomials of order \ell are defined respectively by When x=0 they reduce to the Bernoulli and Euler numbers of order \ell : For this and other properties see Milne-Thomson ( 1933 , pp. 126–153) or Nörlund ( 1924 , pp. 144–162) . For extensions of B^{(\ell)}_{n}\left(x\right) to complex values of x , n , and \ell , and also for uniform asymptotic expansions for large x and large n , see Temme ( 1995b ) and López and Temme ( 1999b , 2010b ) . Here s\left(n,m\right) again denotes the Stirling number of the first kind. B^{(x)}_{n} is a polynomial in x of degree n . (This notation is consistent with ( 24.16.3 ) when x=\ell .) Let \chi be a primitive Dirichlet character \mod f (see § 27.8 ). Then f is called the conductor of \chi . Generalized Bernoulli numbers and polynomials belonging to \chi are defined by Let \chi_{0} be the trivial character and \chi_{4} the unique (nontrivial) character with f=4 ; that is, \chi_{4}(1)=1 , \chi_{4}(3)=-1 , \chi_{4}(2)=\chi_{4}(4)=0 . Then" Equation 24.16.3 on the page has alt text "\displaystyle B^{(\ell)}_{n}". Equation 24.16.4 on the page has alt text "\left(\frac{\ln\left(1+t\right)}{t}\right)^{\ell}=\ell\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac% {B^{(\ell+n)}_{n}}{\ell+n}\frac{t^{n}}{n!},". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
